cohort: 109 nulliparous women with a prolonged active second stage of labor (active pushing lasting more than 120 minutes)
finding: In nulliparous women with prolonged second stage of labor, transabdominal and transperineal intrapartum ultrasound parameters, particularly the midline angle and head-symphysis distance, can predict the likelihood of spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Several transabdominal and transperineal ultrasound parameters were able to predict the likelihood of spontaneous vaginal delivery versus operative delivery in nulliparous women experiencing a prolonged second stage of labor.
